zh: 这张图，你觉得能一笔画完吗？
en: Could you trace this whole diagram in one continuous stroke?

zh: 每条线，只走一次。
en: Follow every line exactly once.

zh: 总有一条，留在最后。
en: One line always remains at the end.

zh: 1999年，两位心理学家问：
en: In 1999, two psychologists asked:

zh: 你做得怎样，又觉得自己做得怎样？
en: How well did you do, and how well do you think you did?

zh: 低分组实际只超过约12%的人；
en: The lowest-scoring group actually outperformed about 12% of people;

zh: 却以为，自己超过了约62%。
en: yet believed they had outperformed about 62%.

zh: 做对一道题，需要知识。
en: Solving a problem takes knowledge.

zh: 看出自己哪里错了，也可能需要它。
en: Spotting your own mistakes may take it too.

zh: 缺的知识，可能让错误也藏了起来。
en: Missing knowledge may also hide the mistake.

zh: 回到这张图：经过路口，要一进一出。
en: Back to this diagram: at a junction, one line in, one line out.

zh: 三条线，总有一条落单。
en: With three lines, one is always left unpaired.

zh: 这种路口，只能留给起点或终点。
en: Such a junction must be a start or an end.

zh: 起点和终点，只有两个。
en: There are only two: a start and an end.

zh: 这样的路口，这里却有四个。
en: But this diagram has four such junctions.

zh: 原来，它根本画不完。
en: So it cannot be traced under these rules.

zh: 学到的，也是一把判断自己的尺。
en: What you learn also becomes a measure of your own judgment.

zh: 但别急着，拿它给别人贴标签。
en: But do not rush to use it to label other people.

zh: 分组与测量，也可能放大差距。
en: Grouping and measurement may also amplify the gap.

zh: 后来的智力研究，结果并不一致。
en: Later studies of intelligence did not all agree.

zh: 偏差有多大，还要看任务与方法。
en: The size of the bias depends on the task and the method.

zh: 再看这张图，你先数了路口。
en: Look again: this time, you count the junctions first.

zh: 少一条线，会怎样？
en: What happens if we remove one line?

zh: 先提出判断，再让结果检验它。
en: Make a prediction, then let the result test it.

zh: 所以，觉得自己会了，先做一次验证。
en: So when you think you can do it, put that judgment to a test.

zh: 看见差距，再用反馈修正自己的判断。
en: Notice the gap, then use feedback to revise your judgment.
